title: Money with operators
description:
Write `public readonly record struct Money(long Cents, string Currency)` with:

- `+` and `-` between two amounts of the same currency; different currencies throw `InvalidOperationException`.
- `*` by an `int` (either side).
- `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` for the same currency (different currencies throw `InvalidOperationException`).
- `ToString()` giving `"12.50 EUR"` (negative amounts as `"-3.05 USD"`).

```csharp
var a = new Money(1250, "EUR");
Console.WriteLine(a + new Money(75, "EUR"));   // 13.25 EUR
Console.WriteLine(3 * a);                       // 37.50 EUR
```
hints: `l with { Cents = ... }` copies a record struct with one field changed, keeping the currency.
A small private helper that throws when the currencies differ keeps every operator one line long. `{abs % 100:00}` pads the cents to two digits.
